content.comment_body: Hello everyone, We're collaborating with a software company on a project. At a certain phase, they need to change a variable in my program; specifically, this variable is a counter value. What steps do I need to take? Should I install any additional software on Windows to accomplish this?

Hello [user_name], To program the [product_name] logic controllers, you need [product_name] program software. There's a trial version available for download, but only the full version (article number: [article_no]) allows transferring projects. You can order from the official distributor or reach out to a [company_name] sales representative.

Hello, I've used [product_name] and the associated programming software for a long time and am working on a new project. I believe the [product_name] Access Tool provides a simple way to import data into [product_name] from a PC.

There are three main methods I know for changing parameters in a running [product_name] program. One is using a web browser, if it’s one of the latest model versions. Another is the S7 protocol used for device communication. The third is via Modbus TCP/IP, which is also implemented by other companies. If there is a Windows API available (I’m not aware of one), that might be the only method for custom programs to communicate with [product_name]. [user_name] (translated with Google)
Is it possible to use the simple web server with [version_no] (version 8.0 - 8.3)?

Importing data from [product_name] to PC using Access Tool is possible. However, exporting data from PC to [product_name] (for changing a value) is not supported via the Access Tool. The easiest approach is through the simple web server.

Hi, With the Access Tool, reading data is possible but writing is not. As mentioned, I’ll try accessing and modifying data via a web browser, though it seems complex. Ideally, an application running on the Tablet PC should be able to change the value automatically. Hopefully, we’ll discover a suitable solution. Thank you all for your suggestions.
Your explanations are a bit general. Please upload your [product_name] program in a ZIP file and specify exactly which value you want to change through the web server.

Hello [user_name], I’m sharing the program here, and our LWE program will follow later. Currently, I modify block B014 via web browser (VW 0) manually, but I want a computer application to do it automatically. I suspected the Access Tool might work, but it doesn’t. The password for the LWE program is 0000.
You’re using the extended web server. I tested your LWE project with the [product_name] program, and it works for changing the counter value via the extended web server.

Thank you for your interest. I shared this method with our business partner. I’m still interested in sending data from a Windows PC to [product_name] using Modbus TCP/IP. Do I need a Windows tool for this, or is there a sample application available?

I haven’t encountered any ready-made software to automatically send values to [product_name]. This is quite a specialized task. The application would need to connect to [product_name] and transfer the desired values via Ethernet TCP/IP using either the S7 or Modbus TCP/IP protocols. So, a custom program likely needs to be developed.

Hi, I think it’s possible, but I am not aware of any dedicated Windows/[product_name] app. Generally, you need software on the PC capable of communicating via S7 or Modbus TCP. Configure it to read/write to/from [product_name] (default I/O or VM-Memory). On [product_name], you can access default supported data types: inputs, outputs, flags, and VM-Memory (both digital and analog). Enable and configure the connection and create the appropriate program on [product_name]. Many smart home automation setups utilize a Raspberry Pi with Node-RED and S7 or Modbus TCP for this kind of communication. Some SCADA systems also support these protocols, though SCADA solutions can be expensive for simple [product_name] applications. Alternatively, use the built-in user-defined web server with the LWE, configuring a web page, and access it via a standard web browser on PC. This method is free, as the web server is part of the [product_name] software. The main limitation is the number of simultaneous connections allowed, which depends on the browser—only Firefox lets you limit connection counts. If the LWE features are insufficient, you can edit the source code of the generated HTML page as needed, but you’ll need some expertise. Perhaps your software partner can assist. Hope this helps.

Thank you for your help. I’m currently handling this via the web server, and as stated, I’m working with HTML to process responses. Connection drops might pose a problem. I believe direct Modbus TCP/IP communication from the PC offers the most reliable solution. I haven’t found a definitive Windows-side answer yet. I feel that [company_name] should provide ready-made software for this. As automation and PCs must interact securely, Modbus protocol seems to be the best option.

Indeed, this task is challenging if you want to ‘just send a value.’ There are applications available, but you’ll need to check which options fit your requirements. STEP 7 is a universal software choice for this. Node-RED, AWS, MQTT, and others are possible solutions. [company_name] does offer SCADA software for such needs, but it’s costly since it uses S7 protocol.

Keep in mind, HTML interactions only persist as long as the page is active on your screen. You are correct. LWE displays the code needed to communicate with [product_name] and modify values, but only while the HTML page is open. This could be a good learning path. As stated earlier, it’s a complex challenge.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are seeking ways to remotely adjust variable values—mainly a counter—in a [product_name] controller using a Windows PC. The discussion highlights that [product_name] programming software is needed for setup, but transferring variables during runtime is not supported through the Access Tool. The web server interface comes up as an alternative; however, users consider it either insufficient or too manual for seamless data modification from external software.
analysis.user_expectations: Users desire a simple way to change variable values on a running [product_name] controller from an external Windows application without manual user intervention.
